source.security_rationale: In FFmpeg libavcodec/escape124.c (commit 3d7817048cb387de87600f2152075f78b37b60a6, Ticket 1629), the upstream security fix addresses an integer overflow leading to excessive memory allocation. In the vulnerable code, can_safely_read(gb, bits) declared parameter 'bits' as int (32-bit signed), while caller unpack_codebook computed 'size * 34' where 'size' was unsigned. The complete upstream fix consists of two changes: (1) in can_safely_read, widening the parameter type from 'int' to 'uint64_t' so that large bit counts do not evaluate improperly against get_bits_left(gb); and (2) in unpack_codebook, promoting the multiplication to 'size * 34L'. This contrastive demonstration pair captures exclusively change (1) — widening parameter 'bits' from 'int' to 'uint64_t' in can_safely_read — while change (2) ('size * 34L') resides in caller unpack_codebook outside this function pair. Reviewers must evaluate this demonstration in the context of the full upstream commit diff, acknowledging that the demonstrated snippet reflects the parameter type widening component of the integer overflow defense.
